chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And they killed the prophets without right.' He said: 'By Allah, they did not kill them with their swords, but they publicized their secrets and exposed them, so they killed them.'
ai.seo_question: How did the enemies kill the prophets according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) offers a nuanced exegesis of the phrase 'killed the prophets,' interpreting it not as physical execution by swords, but as the spiritual and social death caused by the publicizing of their inner secrets (*sir*) and truths. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the vulnerability of the Imams and Prophets to the loss of their esoteric knowledge (*taqiyya* or *kashf*) through the actions of their followers or enemies, linking the concept of 'publicising' directly to the erosion of their divine authority.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:61] and killed the Prophets unjustly. So heasws said: ‘But, by Allahazwj, they did not kill themas by their swords, but they publicised theiras secrets and exposed upon themas, so they killed themas’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama’a from abu Basir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

About the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘. . . for unjustly murdering the prophets . . .,’ [3:112] the Imam said, ‘By Allah, they did not murder them with their swords but they publicized their secrets, spread them against the prophets who then were murdered.’”
